title: Business Requirements Document — AI-Driven Requirement Engineering Assistant

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body: Northfield Retail Group, operating 46 physical stores across the western region, has approved funding for 'NovaCart,' a customer-facing e-commerce platform. The strategic rationale for this initiative is to establish a direct-to-consumer digital sales channel, which is currently absent, to break the revenue cap imposed by physical footfall and store operating hours. The platform aims to recapture market share lost to regional competitors with online storefronts and to reduce the high volume of inbound customer service calls related to order status by providing self-service tracking. NovaCart is positioned as the company's primary growth channel over the next three fiscal years, with a projected contribution of 18% to total company revenue within 24 months of launch. The system will also provide store operations staff with a unified administrative console for catalogue, inventory, and fulfillment management, laying the foundation for future loyalty and personalization initiatives.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body:
The business objectives are defined to ensure the platform meets specific performance and adoption targets. 

**Objective OBJ-01:** Enable customers to create an account and authenticate securely. 
*Success Metric:* Registration completion rate ≥ 70%.

**Objective OBJ-02:** Provide fast, relevant product discovery. 
*Success Metric:* Search-to-product-view conversion ≥ 40%.

**Objective OBJ-03:** Provide a frictionless cart and checkout experience. 
*Success Metric:* Cart abandonment rate ≤ 65% within 6 months.

**Objective OBJ-04:** Give customers visibility of order status and history. 
*Success Metric:* Order-status call volume reduced by 30%.

**General Success Criteria:**
1. Platform goes live within the approved budget and timeline.
2. Customers can independently register, search, purchase, and track orders without contacting support.
3. Store operations staff can manage products, inventory, and orders from a single administration console.
4. No Sev-1 defects open at go-live; UAT sign-off obtained from all business stakeholders.

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries (In/Out of Scope)
sections.body:
**In Scope:**
The initial release is strictly limited to the four core customer journeys agreed upon with the client:
1. Registration and login.
2. Product search and details.
3. Cart and checkout.
4. Order tracking and history.

Additionally, the scope includes a single administrative system for store operations to manage catalogue, inventory, and fulfillment.

**Out of Scope:**
1. Loyalty programs, personalization engines, and marketplace initiatives (identified as future foundations but not part of the initial release).
2. Storage of cardholder data locally (mandated by PCI-DSS compliance constraints).
3. Any features beyond the four core customer journeys listed above.

**Operational Boundaries:**
The solution must be delivered within a fixed six-month timeline. The platform must integrate with a third-party payment gateway (contracted separately) and existing internal store inventory APIs.

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body:
The following stakeholders have been identified with specific roles and responsibilities:

1. **Arvind Deshmukh (Client Sponsor):** Funds the project and owns the overall business outcome.
2. **Rina Sinha (Product Owner):** Owns the product backlog, prioritization, and final sign-off.
3. **Store Operations Manager (Business SME):** Represents the inventory and fulfillment process.
4. **Customer Service Lead (Business SME):** Represents the order management and customer support processes.

*Note: The source document excerpt is truncated regarding the full list of stakeholders. Additional governance personas (e.g., IT Security, Legal/Compliance) are not explicitly defined in the provided text and require stakeholder input to complete the governance model.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body:
**Assumptions:**
1. The client will provide product catalogue data (SKU, price, images, description) in a structured format prior to the development of the catalogue module.
2. A third-party payment gateway will be contracted separately and made available for integration by Sprint 3.
3. Store inventory systems can expose stock levels through an existing internal API.

**Operational Constraints:**
1. **Timeline:** The solution must be delivered within a fixed six-month timeline agreed with the sponsor.
2. **Compliance:** The platform must comply with PCI-DSS requirements; no cardholder data may be stored locally.
3. **Scope Limitation:** The initial release is limited to the four core customer journeys: registration/login, product search/details, cart/checkout, and order tracking/history.

**Domain Profile Conflict Note:** The domain profile specifies healthcare compliance frameworks (HIPAA, GDPR, HL7 FHIR, DICOM) and NFR benchmarks (AES-256, RTO < 1h, RPO < 5min). However, the source document describes a retail e-commerce platform (NovaCart) for Northfield Retail Group. This discrepancy is a critical ambiguity. If the system is indeed a retail platform, healthcare compliance frameworks may not apply. If the system is intended to handle healthcare data (e.g., selling medical devices with patient data), the healthcare constraints must be enforced. Stakeholder clarification is required to resolve this conflict.

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body:
**Identified Risks (from Audit):**
1. **Lack of Specific PHI Encryption Standards (HIGH):** The document mentions 'password encryption' and 'privacy of medical information' but fails to specify encryption standards for PHI at rest or in transit. Mitigation: Specify AES-256 for data at rest and TLS 1.2+ for data in transit.
2. **Absence of Audit Trail Immutability (HIGH):** The document lists 'audit logs' but does not define integrity or immutability. Mitigation: Specify append-only storage or blockchain-based ledger for audit logs.
3. **Missing Interoperability Standards (HIGH):** The document mentions 'electronic medical records' and 'laboratory test reports' but does not reference HL7 FHIR or DICOM. Mitigation: Integrate HL7 FHIR R4 and DICOM standards.
4. **Undefined Disaster Recovery Benchmarks (MEDIUM):** The document mentions 'backup/recovery' but provides no RTO or RPO. Mitigation: Define RTO < 1 hour and RPO < 5 minutes.
5. **Ambiguous RBAC Granularity (MEDIUM):** The document lists roles but does not specify access granularity. Mitigation: Define a detailed RBAC matrix mapping roles to CRUD permissions.

**Compliance Baseline:**
- **PCI-DSS:** Mandatory for the retail e-commerce aspect (no local cardholder data).
- **HIPAA/GDPR:** Applicable if the system handles PHI. The source document's mention of 'medical information' and 'electronic medical records' suggests potential healthcare data handling, but this is not explicitly confirmed. Stakeholder input is required to determine if HIPAA/GDPR compliance is mandatory.
- **HL7 FHIR/DICOM:** Required if the system interoperates with other healthcare systems. The source document does not specify this, but the audit flags it as a gap.

**Open Items for Stakeholder Input:**
1. Clarify if the system handles PHI or is purely a retail e-commerce platform.
2. Confirm if healthcare compliance frameworks (HIPAA, GDPR, HL7 FHIR, DICOM) are applicable.
3. Define RTO/RPO benchmarks if the system is healthcare-critical.
4. Specify audit log immutability requirements.
5. Define RBAC granularity for all roles.
6. Provide a threat model and security architecture.
7. Define data retention and archival policies.

_source_audit.summary: The document provides a high-level functional overview of a Hospital Management System (HMS), listing core modules (EMR, Billing, Pharmacy, etc.) and a suggested tech stack (React, FastAPI/Node, PostgreSQL). However, it lacks the technical depth, specific compliance mappings (HIPAA/GDPR), data standards (HL7 FHIR/DICOM), and non-functional benchmarks required for a production-grade healthcare system. It reads as a generic software requirements outline rather than a rigorous architectural specification.

risk_factors.title: Lack of Specific PHI Encryption Standards
risk_factors.description: The document mentions 'password encryption' and 'privacy of medical information' but fails to specify encryption standards for Protected Health Information (PHI) at rest or in transit. It does not mandate AES-256 for data at rest or TLS 1.2+ for data in transit, which are HIPAA Security Rule requirements.
risk_factors.mitigation: Explicitly specify AES-256 encryption for all PHI fields in the database and TLS 1.2/1.3 for all API communications. Define key management strategies (e.g., KMS) for encryption keys.

verification.claim: Risk: Lack of Specific PHI Encryption Standards — The document mentions 'password encryption' and 'privacy of medical information' but fails to specify encryption standards for Protected Health Information (PHI) at rest or in transit. It does not mandate AES-256 for data at rest or TLS 1.2+ for data in transit, which are HIPAA Security Rule requirements.
verification.reason: Source mentions password encryption and privacy but gives no PHI encryption standards.

risk_factors.title: Absence of Audit Trail Immutability
risk_factors.description: The document lists 'audit logs' as a feature but does not define the integrity or immutability of these logs. In healthcare, audit trails must be tamper-proof to satisfy HIPAA and GDPR accountability requirements.
risk_factors.mitigation: Specify that audit logs must be written to an append-only storage system or blockchain-based ledger to ensure immutability. Define retention periods and access controls for audit logs.

verification.claim: Risk: Absence of Audit Trail Immutability — The document lists 'audit logs' as a feature but does not define the integrity or immutability of these logs. In healthcare, audit trails must be tamper-proof to satisfy HIPAA and GDPR accountability requirements.
verification.reason: Audit logs are listed without any immutability or tamper‑proof guarantees.

risk_factors.title: Missing Interoperability Standards (HL7 FHIR/DICOM)
risk_factors.description: The document mentions 'electronic medical records' and 'laboratory test reports' but does not reference HL7 FHIR or DICOM standards. This creates a siloed system that cannot easily exchange data with other healthcare providers or imaging devices.
risk_factors.mitigation: Integrate HL7 FHIR R4 for clinical data exchange and DICOM for medical imaging. Define API endpoints that conform to FHIR resources (Patient, Observation, MedicationRequest).

verification.claim: Risk: Missing Interoperability Standards (HL7 FHIR/DICOM) — The document mentions 'electronic medical records' and 'laboratory test reports' but does not reference HL7 FHIR or DICOM standards. This creates a siloed system that cannot easily exchange data with other healthcare providers or imaging devices.
verification.reason: EMR and lab reports are described but HL7 FHIR or DICOM are not referenced.

risk_factors.title: Undefined Disaster Recovery Benchmarks
risk_factors.description: The document mentions 'backup/recovery' and 'high availability' but provides no specific Recovery Time Objective (RTO) or Recovery Point Objective (RPO). For a hospital system, downtime can be life-threatening.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define RTO < 1 hour and RPO < 5 minutes. Specify active-active or active-passive database replication strategies to meet these benchmarks.

verification.claim: Risk: Undefined Disaster Recovery Benchmarks — The document mentions 'backup/recovery' and 'high availability' but provides no specific Recovery Time Objective (RTO) or Recovery Point Objective (RPO). For a hospital system, downtime can be life-threatening.
verification.reason: Backup/recovery and high availability are mentioned without RTO/RPO metrics.

risk_factors.title: Ambiguous Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) Granularity
risk_factors.description: The document lists roles (Admin, Doctor, Nurse, etc.) but does not specify the granularity of access. For example, it is unclear if a Nurse can view financial billing data or if a Doctor can modify another Doctor's clinical notes.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define a detailed RBAC matrix mapping each role to specific CRUD permissions for each data entity (e.g., Patient, Invoice, Prescription). Implement least-privilege principles.

verification.claim: Risk: Ambiguous Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) Granularity — The document lists roles (Admin, Doctor, Nurse, etc.) but does not specify the granularity of access. For example, it is unclear if a Nurse can view financial billing data or if a Doctor can modify another Doctor's clinical notes.
verification.reason: Roles are enumerated but no detail on access granularity for each role.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.context: The document states 'secure authentication, password encryption, session management, HTTPS' but does not specify multi-factor authentication (MFA) or specific password complexity policies.
conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Mandate MFA for all staff roles. Specify password complexity rules (e.g., NIST 800-63B) and session timeout durations (e.g., 15 minutes of inactivity).

verification.claim: Ambiguity: Vague Definition of 'Secure Authentication' — The document states 'secure authentication, password encryption, session management, HTTPS' but does not specify multi-factor authentication (MFA) or specific password complexity policies.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.issue: Unclear Data Ownership and Consent Management
conflicts_and_ambiguities.context: The document mentions 'patient registration' and 'privacy of medical information' but does not address patient consent for data sharing or GDPR rights (right to erasure, portability).
conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Implement a consent management module that tracks patient consent for data usage. Define workflows for handling GDPR data subject access requests (DSAR) and right to be forgotten.

Client Business Idea 
1.1 Business Objective 
Northfield Retail Group operates 46 physical stores across the western region and currently has no direct-to-
consumer digital sales channel. Management has approved funding for NovaCart, a customer-facing e-commerce 
platform that will allow shoppers to browse, purchase and track products online while giving store operations staff a 
single system to manage catalogue, inventory and fulfilment. The platform is expected to become the company's 
primary growth channel over the next three fiscal years. 
1.2 Current Business Problem 
Sales today are confined to physical footfall, which caps revenue to store catchment areas and store operating hours. 
Customers who want to check stock, compare products or place an order outside of store hours have no channel to 
do so, and the company has already lost measurable market share to regional competitors that operate online 
storefronts. Customer service also fields a high volume of phone enquiries about order status because there is no 
self-service tracking capability. 
1.3 Expected Business Value 
● A new digital revenue stream projected to contribute 18% of total company revenue within 24 months of 
launch. 
● Reduction in inbound customer service call volume through self-service order tracking and order history. 
● Improved inventory visibility across the store network through a unified product catalogue. 
● A foundation for future loyalty, personalisation and marketplace initiatives. 
1.4 Business Goals 
● Launch a functioning e-commerce storefront within two fiscal quarters. 
● Provide customers a self-service channel for registration, ordering and tracking. 
● Give store operations a single administrative system for catalogue and order management.
